 Line-ups

 Summary
 Tomos Williams , Dewi Lake and Archie Griffin cross for first-half Wales tries, with New Zealand responding through Cortez Ratima , Wallace Sititi and Fehi Fineanganofo 
 Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit put Wales back in front after the break
 Wales have not beaten the All Blacks since 1953
 Wales make four starting changes from the victory over Japan in Cardiff
 Taine Basham makes his first Wales Test start since 2022
 New Zealand have made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland at Murrayfield
 Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time

 Is it on? IS IT ON?

 Converted try: Wales 28-21 New Zealand published at 43 mins 43 mins 
 Eddie James (con: Sam Costelow) 
 Louis Rees-Zammit has been immense. The wing carries hard into the 22, then Wales fling it to the left for flanker James Botham.
 Basham with a big carry, then Botham again, followed by Nicky Smith, Basham again, Botham again.
 Wales are within a metre.
 Tomos Williams tries to snipe and is stopped but then the scrum-half pings a pass to the left wing, where Eddie James has a run-in.
 Costelow converts from the left touchline and Wales believe again!
 Image source, Getty Images

 Can Wales go the distance? published at 15:10 GMT 15:10 GMT 
 HT: Wales 21-21 New Zealand 
 Ian Gough 
Former Wales international on BBC Radio Wales 
 Wales came out with an intent to play, they need to come out with the same intent, keeping the pressure on. 
 They are playing superbly, but any mistake is punished, and we've seen that in this first half.
 It's heart breaking that we finished the first half like that, each team is making mistakes from set pieces. 
 Wales have intensity at the breakdown, they are looking as good as New Zealand out there.
 But are Wales used to going this distance? They will be tired in the second half.

 What a weekend we're having published at 15:08 GMT 15:08 GMT 
 HT: Wales 21-21 New Zealand 
 Image source, Reuters This round of action kicked off in sensational fashion last night when France won a classic against South Africa in Paris.
 The quality of that Test between two World Cup hopefuls will not be matched this weekend - or will it?
 Nonetheless, today's action got under way in Genoa in a ground that brings back memories of Ruud Gullit, David Platt, Roberto Mancini and Attilio Lombardo in action for Sampdoria.
 It wasn't a classic but it was tense, with Argentina holding on to beat Italy 19-14. Paolo Garbisi had a shocker for the Azzurri by kicking the ball dead with the clock in the red, trying to go right into the corner.
 Next up after this game is Eddie Jones’ return to Twickenham when Japan take on England (16:40 GMT), who are aiming to back up their thrashing of Australia.
 It will be a surprise if that’s not a home win and the same applies in Dublin tonight where Ireland host Fiji (20:10 GMT).
 Will it be tighter in Edinburgh tomorrow? Hopefully.
 The round is finished off by Scotland and Australia aiming to bounce back from disappointments against the All Blacks and England respectively (15:10 GMT).

 HT: Wales 21-21 New Zealand 
 Gareth Griffiths 
BBC Sport Wales at Principality Stadium 
 The last time Wales were not behind against New Zealand was in 2016.
 After leading 14-0 and 21-7 it could have been better for Steve Tandy’s side at the interval.
 But not many Welsh fans would have predicted they would be level with New Zealand after 40 minutes in Cardiff.
 Let’s see what happens now in the second half.

 And Matt in Edinburgh, those in Scotland know the quality of the 'All Blacks' B team' after results through the years!

 HT: Wales 21-21 New Zealand 
 You can't coach Welshness. New Zealand might have the Haka, but we've got heart and grit. The boys are fronting up, emptying the tank and asking serious questions out wide. The All Blacks have been dragged into an old-fashioned arm wrestle in the cauldron.
